## Summary so far

I fixed the confirmed cross-tenant governance bypass in PR #561 and pushed corrective commits to the same branch (`worker/task-20260726-035742-phase3-business-rule-permission-policy-c`).

**Root cause & fix:** `getPromptLifecycleRule()` resolved `min_eval_pass_rate`/`min_canary_duration_hours`/`eval_daily_budget_usd` through the org-override chain even though `prompt_templates`/`prompt_versions`/`prompt_eval_runs` are platform-wide tables with no `orgId`. I verified against `schema.ts`'s own design comments that these tables are intentionally platform-wide, service_role-governed catalogs — so I made the governance rules **platform-only**: `getPromptLifecycleRule()` and `checkPromptEvalBudget()` no longer take an `orgId` parameter at all and only ever read the `scope_type='platform'` row, never the org/project/client override chain. This closes the exploit where a same-org rank-5 admin could zero out canary/eval-pass-rate gates for a same-org `veridian_admin` to bypass on any shared template.

**Also fixed:**
- `checkPromptPolicyDeny()`'s org-scoped-ABAC-vs-platform-resource mismatch — documented as an intentional, deny-only limitation (can only over-restrict, never escalate) rather than building a new platform-scope ABAC capability out of scope for this fix.
- PII credit-card regex tightened with a real Luhn checksum, eliminating false positives on ordinary long digit runs while still catching real card numbers.
- Added `prompt-governance-gates.test.ts` (DB-mocked) covering `runLifecycleTransitionGates` and `checkPromptEvalBudget`, including explicit regression tests reproducing the PR #561 cross-tenant escalation scenario.

**Verification:** `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, full `bun test` suite: **2029 pass / 0 fail** across 166 files.

Commits `b97bdac5`, `8001e478`, `3bb91a03` pushed to the PR branch. CI is now running on the latest push — I'll report back once it completes.
